members.name: Ananya
members.thread: A product design studio from the living room: briefs, boards, contracts and invoices.

members.name: Rohan
members.thread: An indie developer in the stair study, beside the grand piano.

character.lede: A desert-modern city villa joins blue-grey fieldstone and white render under stepped brown standing-seam roofs. A black-framed portal opens onto a planted court, and the back yard has a pool and a fire bowl.

spots.line: A grand piano, a writing desk and a laptop share the stair study.
An L-shaped sectional, a fireplace and a television face one wall.
A washer, a dryer and a counter fill the laundry room.

facts.style: Desert-modern city villa: blue-grey fieldstone and white render, a stone-and-glass west block showing its floating stair and grand piano through a timber spandrel band, a black-framed portal in the stone wall onto an open planted court, stepped brown standing-seam mono-pitches over black fascias, a resort back yard with terraced timber decks, an L-shaped pool, a spa gazebo and palms

character.truths: The Core sits on a desk in the Living Room. The living room has a fireplace and a television. The kitchen has an island. A grand piano stands in the stair study. Pool, fire bowl, pergola and string lights outside.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
opencut: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Footage stays in the browser's storage on the editing machine, not on the Core
Compose points NEXT_PUBLIC_MARBLE_API_URL at api.marblecms.com with a disabled key: an outside call to check
No QA run and no screenshot
lunalytics: Setup wizard asks for email and username on first visit
Do not claim a public status page
Overlaps Uptime Kuma (another slice): one uptime monitor per household
tldraw: not open source (tldraw licence; a production watermark shows)
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
vaultwarden: [note] Bitwarden-compatible server, unofficial. Do not say "Bitwarden".
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
penpot: Five containers (frontend, backend, exporter, Postgres, Redis).
QA screenshot is the log-in page: reject.
Listing images show community library tiles: marketing.
hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core
Heavy for a client tool: three containers
aider: [cloud-link] The Hub injects its own model endpoint, so it needs no cloud key. A model override field can point it at another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; leave it on the Hub model. A coding agent is private only on the C
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. Every edit is a git commit, which is the approval step: the person reviews and can undo it with git.
[note] The browser interface is marked experimental upstream. Do not call it finished.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pi-hole: [claims] Network-wide blocking at DNS. Do not call it parental control or promise safety.
Blocks ad, tracker and bad domains at DNS: not parental control and no promise of safety
Unblocked lookups are forwarded to an upstream resolver (the upstream demo dashboard lists a public DNS, dns.google), so a DNS provider still sees them and it is not offline
Overlaps AdGuard Home: one per household
espocrm: [note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
cryptgeon: Notes live only in RAM: a restart of the app wipes every unread note
Do not repeat the listing's encryption wording (sec-absolute); say a note opens once and is gone
Overlaps Enclosed and PrivateBin: one burn-after-reading tool per household
airtrail: Logbook and statistics, not live flight tracking (listing short_desc says "flight tracking")
Does not claim live flight status; story must say logbook
homebox: [note] Barcode and Open Food Facts lookups call outside services.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Analytics are switched off in the manifest (good)
baikal: Whoever opens the app first runs the install wizard and sets the admin password
Overlaps Radicale and Nextcloud calendars: one calendar server per household
readeck: listing says securely: do not repeat
QA shot is the first-run form
